credits.source: Photograph of the zellige dado of the Bou Inania madrasa, Fès (Wikimedia Commons, File:Bou_inania_DSCF2978.jpg)
credits.note: The design was read from this photo; the construction is our own reconstruction, not a published one, drawn the way Samira Mian builds her rosettes: each set of twelve lines through a corner already drawn, touching one circle about O.

steps.text: Draw a circle about the centre O through A, and the horizontal line through both. A is halfway to the next rosette: the rosettes of this wall sit on a square grid, two radii apart.

Draw the vertical through O. Through A and through the top of the circle draw lines at right angles to these: they are lines of the grid, and where they cross is the corner K of the tile, where an eight-pointed star will sit.

Divide the circle into twelve: with the compass still open to OA, put its point on A and mark where it cuts the circle at 60°. Join O to that mark, and halve the angles between the lines through O, so you have a line through O every 15°.
Join A to the top of the circle. Through the point of the circle at 45°, draw a line at 60°. Where the two lines cross is the first corner of the rosette.

Through the first corner, draw two lines: one at right angles to the 0° direction, one at right angles to the 30° direction. Turn each round the rosette: two sets of twelve lines, each set touching one circle about O. The second set joins points of the first circle 150° apart, like the star lines of a simple rosette.

Open the compass from O to the corner K. Put its point on the copy of the first corner down and to the left of O, and mark where the arc crosses the horizontal on the right: this is the outer tip of the rosette.
Through the outer tip, draw a line at 105° and turn it round: the set that will close the shields.
Through the point of a small star, where the last lines cross, draw the two sets that cross there, at right angles to the 0° and the 30° directions.
Through the first corner again, draw two more sets: one that closes the shields, and a helper that fixes the corner beside the outer tip.
Through the corner beside the outer tip, draw two sets: one that closes the pentagons, and a helper reaching in towards the centre.
Through the inner end of a petal, draw the set that makes the sides of the petals.
Through the shoulder of a petal, draw two sets: one closes the small kites between the petals, the other runs along the petals’ outer sides.
Through the outer corner of a petal, draw the two sets that make the small stars.
Through the tip of a small kite between two petals, draw the last set: it makes the twelve-pointed star at the centre.

Open the compass from A to the point between two petals at 60°, and draw that circle about O. Where it crosses the horizontal, draw a line at right angles: one side of the twelve-sided rim around the rosette. Copy it round.
Mark the corners of the rim at 15° and 45°, and draw the level line through the 45° corner.

Through K draw the other diagonal. The eight-pointed star at K is two squares: one square’s sides are the rims of the four rosettes around it; the other, turned square has its sides as far from K. Set the compass to that distance (from the rim side to A), draw it about K, and draw the turned square’s sides across the diagonals where the circle cuts them.

The ring around the star is two octagons. The inner one has its square sides through the rim’s 45° corner, the outer one its diagonal side: draw a circle about K through each, and the octagon sides across the grid lines and the diagonals where the circles cut them.
Copy the star and its ring to the other three corners of the tile by turning them a quarter turn at a time about O, together with the grid lines.
Mark the corners of the pattern: every point where two of the lines meet and the pattern turns.
The tile is the square between the four eight-pointed stars.

ink.text: Ink the rosette, its twelve-sided rim, the bands between the rosettes and the eight-pointed stars with their rings.

pattern.text: Repeat the square tile edge to edge: rosettes on a square grid, stars at the corners.
